candidates.source_attribution: Jubilees 36:1 (Isaac's testament (36:1)), trans. R.H. Charles, The Book of Jubilees (Oxford: Clarendon, 1902). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And in the sixth year of this week, in the forty-fourth jubilee, Isaac called his two sons, Esau and Jacob, and they came to him, and he said unto them: my sons, I am going the way of my fathers, to the eternal house where my fathers are' — Isaac's dying-charge frames death as 'the way of my fathers, to the eternal house.' Jubilees presents an explicit intermediate-state-as-fellowship-with-the-departed-righteous doctrine, antecedent to Lk 16:22 (Abraham's bosom) and the Tewahedo prayer 'in the bosom of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob.' The Tewahedo funeral-liturgy phrase 'in the eternal house with the fathers' is the direct verbal-inheritance of Jub 36:1 — the patriarchal-formulary preserved across millennia.

candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And I command you, my sons, that ye love one another, the one his brother as a man loves his own soul, and let each strive in that which he can do for his brother, and do righteousness on the earth between you; and ye shall love one another as your own selves' — Isaac's testament commands love-of-brother-as-one's-own-self, the canonical doubled-witness with Jub 20:2 (Abraham's testament) and Lev 19:18. The Tewahedo's distinctive heavy emphasis on family-and-monastic-community fraternal love (not as innovation but as canonical-patriarchal commandment) draws warrant from the patriarchal-testament triad: Abraham (Jub 20:2), Isaac (Jub 36:7), and the eventual Mosaic codification (Lev 19:18). The Tewahedo monastic Maḫǝbär Qǝddus 'beloved-brothers' charism is the canonical-patriarchal inheritance applied to spiritual-kinship community.
